page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance engineered for enterprise workloads requiring an extreme memory footprint combined with high single-thread clock speeds. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8252C processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz, the system provides 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture. It is populated with 1,536 GB of high-speed DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, offering a 32:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. With no hypervisor layer present, workloads gain direct bare-metal access to CPU hardware capabilities and virtualization flags.

Benchmark evaluation shows exceptional throughput in memory-centric and compute-heavy vector tasks. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 210.08 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 98.02 GB/sec, placing the instance in the upper performance quartile. The server achieved a PassMark CPU score of 49,425.07 and demonstrated strong compiler throughput with a Clang compilation score of 39,257.0. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 31.99 GB/sec. Conversely, without hardware acceleration, text generation benchmarks for large language models remain low, indicating limited utility for neural network inference.

The instance includes a 100 Gbps baseline network interface and is EBS-optimized. However, it provides no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all data persistence relies on external network-attached volumes. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the system delivers high resource density for workloads bottlenecked strictly by RAM capacity and memory bandwidth rather than massive parallel core counts.

Amazon Web Services x2iezn.metal is primarily targeted at in-memory databases like SAP HANA and Redis, large-scale Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tooling, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise relational database management systems that fit entirely within system memory.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by dedicated 24-core, 48-vCPU Intel Xeon 8252C processors reaching clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The platform provides direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead, pairing high-frequency x86_64 compute with an expansive 1,536 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz. Benchmark metrics emphasize superior uncached memory bandwidth of 210.08 GB/sec read and 98.02 GB/sec write, along with top-tier PassMark CPU and Clang software compilation results. The server lacks local storage disks and discrete GPUs, routing persistent I/O over a 100 Gbps network interface to Elastic Block Store. Given the substantial 32 GB memory allocation per vCPU, x2iezn.metal delivers an optimal profile for in-memory databases, electronic design automation, transactional database engines, and high-throughput memory-resident data caching environments.
